name: OpenPro
tagline: An AI layer over project planning: turn a rough brief into structured epics, tasks and status tracking.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core trick here, feeding a messy project brief to a model and getting back a tidy tree of epics and tasks you can drag around, is a solved weekend build. An agent can hand you a local kanban with an LLM planner, SQLite storage and markdown task notes in one long sitting. What it cannot hand you is the boring half: two-way sync with Jira, Linear or GitHub Issues, per-seat permissions, comment threads, notifications that actually reach people, and a mobile view that does not embarrass you in a standup. Public detail on this product is thin, so treat the verdict as a judgment on the category rather than a line-by-line teardown. If you plan solo, build it. If a team lives in it, the sync and collaboration gap will eat you.
coreLoopDIY: Paste a project brief, get an LLM-generated epic and task breakdown you can edit, reorder and track on a local kanban board backed by SQLite.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic) in .env
Local disk for the SQLite file
Willingness to be the only user
whatYouLose: Two-way sync with Jira, Linear, GitHub Issues and whatever else the team already lives in
Multi-user accounts, roles, mentions and comment threads
Mobile and offline access that is not just a browser tab on a phone
Notifications, digests and anything that nudges people without you doing it
Someone else's problem when the schema needs to change or the model output drifts
moatNotes: Planning tools rarely win on the planner. They win on being the place the tickets already are, and on the hundred small interactions that make a board feel alive.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a project tool that only you can see is a to-do list with extra steps. Teams pay so the plan is visible, commentable and connected to the tracker engineering actually opens, and so nobody has to babysit an LLM prompt to keep the backlog shaped. The AI breakdown is the demo; the sync, permissions and notification plumbing is the product. A personal build is genuinely useful for solo planning and genuinely useless the moment a second person needs to be accountable to it.
notes: Fine as a solo planning toy, and the moment you add a coworker you have rebuilt half of Linear badly.
prompt:
Build a local-first AI project planner in an empty folder. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/openpro.db
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- Server Actions for all mutations, no separate API layer
- LLM calls server-side only, key read from process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY, loaded from .env.local, committed .env.example with a placeholder

Data model:
- project: id, name, brief (markdown), createdAt
- epic: id, projectId, title, summary, sortOrder
- task: id, epicId, title, detail (markdown), status (backlog | doing | blocked | done), estimate (S | M | L), sortOrder
- No users table. Single implicit local operator.

Features in scope:
1. Project list page: create, rename, delete a project.
2. Project page with a brief editor (plain textarea, markdown, autosaves on blur).
3. "Plan it" button: sends the brief to the LLM with a strict JSON schema and returns epics, each with 3 to 8 tasks. Show a diff-style preview and require an explicit Accept before writing to the database. Never silently overwrite existing epics; offer Append or Replace.
4. Kanban board across the four statuses, drag and drop with dnd-kit, persists sortOrder and status.
5. Task drawer: edit title, detail, estimate, status, delete.
6. "Break this down" on any task: LLM returns 2 to 5 subtasks as sibling tasks in the same epic, same preview-then-accept flow.
7. Export the whole project to a single markdown file. Import the same format back.

Explicitly out of scope: auth, invites, comments, notifications, Jira or Linear or GitHub sync, time tracking, charts, mobile app, Docker.

Requirements:
- Handle malformed LLM JSON: retry once, then show the raw response and let the user fix it by hand.
- Seed script that creates one demo project with epics and tasks so the board is not empty on first run.
- README with setup in under six commands and one paragraph on what this deliberately does not do.
- Keep it to a handful of files. No abstraction layers you cannot justify out loud.
